gap_analysis.regulation_name: Revised National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System Permit Regulation and Effluent Limitations Guidelines for Concentrated Animal Feeding Operations in Response to the Waterkeeper Decision

requirements.requirement_text: The owner or operator of a CAFO must seek coverage under an NPDES permit if the CAFO discharges or proposes to discharge. A CAFO proposes to discharge if it is designed, constructed, operated, or maintained such that a discharge will occur. Specifically, the CAFO owner or operator must either apply for an individual NPDES permit or submit a notice of intent for coverage under an NPDES general permit.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your CAFO discharges or is built and operated in a way that it will discharge into water, you must apply for an NPDES permit.
requirements.deadline: When the CAFO proposes to discharge, unless a later deadline is specified in 122.23(f)
requirements.penalty_info: In all instances, the discharge of a pollutant without a permit is a violation of the Clean Water Act section 301(a) prohibition against unauthorized discharges from point sources.

requirements.requirement_text: A nutrient management plan that at a minimum satisfies the requirements specified in § 122.42(e), including, for all CAFOs subject to 40 CFR part 412, subpart C or subpart D, the requirements of 40 CFR 412.4(c), as applicable.
requirements.plain_language_summary: When applying for a permit, you must include a Nutrient Management Plan (NMP) that meets specific federal requirements.

requirements.requirement_text: Unpermitted Large CAFOs must maintain documentation specified in § 122.42(e)(1)(ix) either on site or at a nearby office, or otherwise make such documentation readily available to the Director or Regional Administrator upon request.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you operate a Large CAFO without a permit, you must keep nutrient management documentation on-site or nearby to prove that any runoff from land application areas qualifies as exempt agricultural stormwater.

requirements.requirement_text: No later than 180 days before the expiration of the permit, or as provided by the Director, any permitted CAFO must submit an application to renew its permit, in accordance with § 122.21(d), unless the CAFO will not discharge or propose to discharge upon expiration of the permit.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you have a permit, you must apply to renew it at least 180 days before it expires, unless your facility will no longer discharge or propose to discharge.
requirements.deadline: No later than 180 days before the expiration of the permit

requirements.requirement_text: In order to certify that a CAFO does not discharge or propose to discharge, the owner or operator of a CAFO must document, based on an objective assessment of the conditions at the CAFO, that the CAFO is designed, constructed, operated, and maintained in a manner such that the CAFO will not discharge
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you choose to voluntarily certify that your CAFO does not discharge, you must document that your facility is designed and operated to prevent discharges, implement a nutrient management plan, and keep these records on-site or nearby.
requirements.penalty_info: Significant penalties for submitting false information, including the possibility of fine and imprisonment for knowing violations.

requirements.requirement_text: If a certification becomes invalid in accordance with paragraph (i)(4) of this section, the CAFO must withdraw its certification within three days of the date on which the CAFO becomes aware that the certification is invalid.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If your voluntary no-discharge certification becomes invalid (for example, if you have a discharge), you must officially withdraw the certification within three days.
requirements.deadline: Within three days of the date on which the CAFO becomes aware that the certification is invalid

requirements.requirement_text: Any permit issued to a CAFO must include a requirement to implement a nutrient management plan that, at a minimum, contains best management practices necessary to meet the requirements of this paragraph and applicable effluent limitations and standards, including those specified in 40 CFR part 412.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you have a CAFO permit, you must implement a nutrient management plan that includes specific best management practices.

requirements.requirement_text: The actual crop(s) planted and actual yield(s) for each field, the actual nitrogen and phosphorus content of the manure, litter, and process wastewater, the results of calculations conducted in accordance with paragraphs (e)(5)(i)(B) and (e)(5)(ii)(D) of this section, and the amount of manure, litter, and process wastewater applied to each field during the previous 12 months; and, for any CAFO that implements a nutrient management plan that addresses rates of application in accordance with paragraph (e)(5)(ii) of this section, the results of any soil testing for nitrogen and phosphorus taken during the preceding 12 months, the data used in calculations conducted in accordance with paragraph (e)(5)(ii)(D) of this section, and the amount of any supplemental fertilizer applied during the previous 12 months.
requirements.plain_language_summary: Permitted CAFOs must submit an annual report detailing the crops planted, yields, manure nutrient content, amount of manure applied, and (if using the narrative rate approach) soil test results and supplemental fertilizer applied over the past 12 months.

requirements.requirement_text: The CAFO owner or operator must provide the Director with the most current version of the CAFO's nutrient management plan and identify changes from the previous version, except that the results of calculations made in accordance with the requirements of paragraphs (e)(5)(i)(B) and (e)(5)(ii)(D) of this section are not subject to the requirements of paragraph (e)(6) of this section.
requirements.plain_language_summary: If you make changes to your nutrient management plan, you must submit the updated plan to the permitting authority and point out what was changed.

requirements.requirement_text: All open surface liquid impoundments must have a depth marker which clearly indicates the minimum capacity necessary to contain the runoff and direct precipitation of the 25-year, 24-hour rainfall event. In the case of new sources subject to effluent limitations established pursuant to § 412.46(a)(1) of this part, all open surface manure storage structures associated with such sources must include a depth marker which clearly indicates the minimum capacity necessary to contain the maximum runoff and direct precipitation associated with the design storm used in sizing the impoundment for no discharge.
requirements.plain_language_summary: You must install a depth marker in all open liquid manure storage structures to clearly show the minimum capacity needed to contain runoff from large storms.

gaps: The facility profile does not confirm if a permit renewal application has been prepared or submitted 180 days prior to the expiration of general permit AWS820156.
There is no documentation confirming the active implementation of the Nutrient Management Plan (NMP) best management practices for the 3,314-head swine operation.
The profile lacks evidence of annual reporting on crop yields, manure nutrient content, and application rates, which were standard requirements prior to the November 2025 NC Supreme Court ruling.
It is unverified whether the facility's open surface liquid impoundments (swine waste lagoons) are equipped with the required depth markers indicating the 25-year, 24-hour rainfall event capacity.
recommended_actions: Check the expiration date of general permit AWS820156 and submit a renewal application no later than 180 days before it expires.
Ensure all best management practices detailed in the facility's Nutrient Management Plan are fully implemented and documented on-site.
Verify that depth markers are installed and clearly visible in all open surface liquid impoundments to monitor the 25-year, 24-hour storm capacity.

Note that while the November 2025 NC Supreme Court ruling struck down annual reporting, groundwater monitoring, and phosphorus testing requirements, continuing to voluntarily compile and maintain annual reports on manure application and crop yields is strongly advised for liability protection.
gap_analysis.summary: Ellwell Lake, operating as a permitted Swine CAFO with 3,314 animals under general permit AWS820156, is subject to several ongoing operational and maintenance requirements. While the facility holds the necessary permit, gaps exist regarding the verification of depth markers in lagoons, active implementation of the Nutrient Management Plan, and permit renewal timelines. Additionally, while the November 2025 NC Supreme Court ruling struck down annual reporting requirements, voluntary compliance is recommended to ensure liability protection.
